title: kv-cache: adaptive spillover + defrag heuristics v30 (memory management & eviction tuning)
author: Eleanor Briggs
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory management: adaptive spillover thresholds, fragmentation-aware eviction priority, background compaction heuristics, and safer paging fallbacks. Reduces tail latency under memory pressure and lowers OOM incidents on high-concurrency workloads.
description:
Motivation: We continue to see tail latency spikes and occasional OOMs in high-concurrency serving workloads when KV cache memory fragments and spillover/paging behavior thrashes. This PR implements a set of coordinated improvements (v30) to memory management and eviction heuristics to reduce fragmentation, prioritize eviction of low-value fragments, and make spillover/paging decisions workload-aware.

Summary of changes:
- Add adaptive spillover controller that adjusts in-memory spill thresholds per GPU based on recent allocation/eviction rate and fragmentation score.
- Implement fragmentation scoring for KV regions: tracks small free runs and hot-key density to bias defragmentation and eviction.
- Introduce compaction-friendly eviction: when fragmentation score > threshold, prefer evicting scattered small entries to enable a background compaction pass.
- Background incremental compaction worker that coalesces free regions with bounded CPU/GPU budget to avoid impacting hot paths.
- Paging fallbacks: improved safe paging path that ensures in-progress requests read required KV slices synchronously before moving pages to host memory. This avoids transient cache misses during spill.
- Metric and tracing additions: fragmentation_score, spillovers_per_min, compaction_cycles, eviction_priority_histogram. Added per-GPU tags for easier routing in dashboards.
- Config knobs: kv.spillover.base_threshold, kv.spillover.adapt_window_ms, kv.compaction.budget_ms, kv.fragmentation.target_run_size. Defaults tuned conservatively to avoid regressions.

Implementation notes:
- The adaptive controller runs in the existing memory manager and samples allocation/eviction events in sliding windows (default 10s). We use an EWMA on allocation rate and fragmentation to avoid oscillation.
- Fragmentation score heuristic: combination of free-run-length tail and hot-key scatter metric. Score is normalized to [0,100].
- Eviction policy: added a two-tier scoring where entries get a base LRU score and a fragmentation penalty; low-value small entries with high scatter are deprioritized for retention.
- Compaction worker is incremental and bounded by kv.compaction.budget_ms per second; it uses a lock-free scan and marks regions for coalescing with a best-effort approach.

Benchmarks and results (internal perf harness):
- 1k concurrent streams, 50B context synthetic workload: 95th p99 latency reduced by ~18% (from 312ms to 256ms).
- OOM events on stress test (100GB model footprint on shared GPU) reduced from 12/day to 0 in 72h run.
- Cost: compaction background CPU usage increased by ~3% on coordinator process under worst-case fragmentation; knobs can disable compaction on CPU constrained deployments.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests for fragmentation scoring and eviction priority added.
- Integration tests: deterministic spillover/paging replay harness extended to validate synchronous read-before-page semantics.
- End-to-end benchmark job added to perf-canary suite (config reference included).
- Stress runs reproduced locally and in perf CI; initial CI run failed intermittently due to a race in the compaction worker marking logic which is fixed in a follow-up commit in this PR.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- Defaults conservative; behavior toggled by runtime flags. No schema changes to on-disk cache format.
- Rollout strategy: enable on Canary pool (10% hosts) for 48h, monitor fragmentation_score and spillover alerts, then ramp to 50% and finally to 100% if stable.
- Fallback: kv.spillover.enable=false will revert to previous behaviour.

Files changed (high level): added controller/metrics and updates to memory manager, eviction logic, compaction worker, tests, and perf harness configs. See list below.

Related: ENG-4123 (kv cache fragmentation incidents), ENG-4280 (perf canary additions).

review_comments: Aisha: Can we bound compaction CPU impact? Suggest kv.compaction.budget_ms and a global flag to pause during high CPU load.\nEleanor: Added budget knob and pause-on-high-cpu, default off. See compaction_worker.cpp commit.
Daniel: The fragmentation score math looks plausible but add unit tests for edge cases (all small runs, all large runs).\nEleanor: Added tests for both extremes and a randomized property test.

Ravi: Concern about eviction oscillation causing repeated paging. Consider hysteresis in the spillover controller.\nEleanor: Implemented EWMA and a minimum hold window to avoid oscillation (kv.spillover.adapt_window_ms).

Marta: CI failure on first run showed a rare race when marking regions for compaction. Is that fixed?\nEleanor: Yes, fixed with an atomic state transition and additional unit test covering concurrent mark/unmark.
discussion_summary: Consensus to land conservative defaults and ramp via canary. Watch fragmentation_score and spillovers_per_min; follow-up to expose more dashboards and a config API for runtime tuning.
notes_for_ops: Dashboard: add fragmentation_score and spillovers_per_min to kv-cache per-GPU dashboard
Alerting: create alert if spillovers_per_min > 100 for 2m or fragmentation_score > 70 for 5m
Rollout: follow the canary plan in description and be prepared to disable kv.spillover.enable if regressions observed
